narrative.overview: VariantLab's interface now opens the way a serious biotech company opens its culture page — with atmosphere, a stated standard, and confidence — then immediately substitutes what a solo technical project actually has in place of a team: verified data, a verified structure, and an honestly reported performance gap. This is a redesign, not a refinement: it replaces the prior Lab Notebook system rather than polishing it, per a user-pinned reference (untillabs.com/our-team). Every borrowed pattern was re-grounded in VariantLab's own real content: the team-photo grid became five real Product Principles; the value-statement cards became the same pattern with real principles as content; the dark 'we value X' banner became 'We report the harder number.' One deliberate deviation from the pinned reference: its category-label-above-statement pattern is dropped, since a kicker/eyebrow above a heading is Impeccable's one hard-banned pattern regardless of what the brief pins.
keyCharacteristics: Committed structural blue at page scale (hero + banner + nav) — a color strategy earned by Persuade-mode permission.
Space Grotesk for every display/heading voice; IBM Plex Sans for body; IBM Plex Mono still exclusively for measured values.
The evidentiary evidence-card system (neutral / verified-teal / dashed-caution-amber) is unchanged and remains load-bearing.
No label ever sits above a heading or bold statement — the statement always carries its own weight.

rules.name: The Semantic Color Rule
rules.body: Verified Teal and Caution Amber never appear decoratively — unchanged across the world replacement.

rules.name: The Committed-Blue Rule
rules.body: Structural blue owns whole regions at page scale (hero, banner, nav) — never a scattered accent on paper sections.

rules.name: The Dashed-Border Rule
rules.body: A dashed border means, specifically and only, 'not test evidence.'

rules.name: The Measurement-Mono Rule
rules.body: IBM Plex Mono renders only measured/computed values.

rules.name: The No-Kicker Rule
rules.body: No label, tag, or eyebrow sits above any heading or bold statement, even where the pinned reference used one.

rules.name: The Flat-By-Design Rule
rules.body: If an element needs to stand out, it earns a background tint or a border — never a shadow.

dos: Do keep the structural blue committed at page scale, never scattered.
Do keep every accent color tied to evidentiary meaning.
Do state a finding in a real sentence with inline Measurement-weight numbers before reaching for a stat-card grid.
Do let a bold statement carry its own weight — no label above it.
donts: Don't add a kicker/eyebrow label above any heading or card statement.
Don't use a dashed border for anything except 'not test evidence.'
Don't fabricate a structural render when the real one isn't available — degrade to an honest text instruction.
Don't put Verified Teal, Caution Amber, or the committed blue on an element that isn't doing one of their specific jobs.
